finding.claim: wipe(User, tenant) never enforces the OWNER role: requireRole() returns a boolean that is discarded, so any caller (including a user with an empty role set) can wipe any tenant via repo.wipe(). Severity HIGH.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled User u and tenant string on the POST /tenants/{t}/wipe route (documented at src/Admin.java:24). Precondition: an authenticated account, or whatever the unseen router permits.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 (irreversible destruction of tenant data).

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) entry point; no check before the sink
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called as a statement; its boolean result is discarded
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws (Javadoc at line 13 states this), so the call has no effect
Contrast: export uses checkRole, which throws SecurityException; wipe is clearly meant to do the same

finding.guards_checked: Only guard in the file is requireRole at line 26, which does not enforce anything. checkRole (line 18) exists but is not used by wipe. No tenant-membership check exists. The HTTP router, authentication middleware, and Repo implementation are not in the repository, so upstream controls are unverified. Triage Checks 2, 4, 10 applied and do not downgrade; Check 13 not applicable (not CRITICAL).

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check in wipe is requireRole at src/Admin.java:26, a bare statement whose boolean is discarded. requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws. checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) exists but wipe does not call it; export at src/Admin.java:32 does. No tenant-membership check exists, and no router, auth middleware, or Repo implementation is in the repository.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: src/Admin.java:26 discards the result of requireRole, which only returns a boolean (src/Admin.java:15), so repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any caller regardless of roles. The attacker is whoever the unseen router admits to POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, so the exploitability caveat is that upstream auth is unverified, but the authorization check inside wipe is a no-op.

finding.claim: Roles are a flat Set<String> with no tenant binding (User at line 4 has no tenant field). If OWNER is a global role, an owner of tenant A can export tenant B. Severity MEDIUM, conditional (HIGH if roles are global).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled tenant string on POST /tenants/{t}/export (src/Admin.java:30) combined with a valid OWNER role held for some other tenant.

trace.note: User record carries roles but no tenant identifier
export(User u, String tenant) takes the tenant from the caller
checkRole(u, "OWNER") checks only that the role string exists, not that it applies to tenant
repo.export(tenant) runs for the requested tenant, which may differ from the caller's tenant

finding.guards_checked: checkRole at line 32 is correctly enforced (throws). No tenant-scope check exists anywhere in this file. Whether roles are per-tenant depends on code outside the repository; if they are scoped before User is constructed, this finding is closed.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws when the role string is missing, so it blocks callers with no OWNER role at all; no tenant-scope check exists in src/Admin.java or anywhere else in the repository.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (User at src/Admin.java:4 has no tenant field, export takes the caller's tenant at line 31, checkRole at line 32 only tests the role string, and repo.export(tenant) runs at line 33), but whether an OWNER role is tenant-scoped is decided by code outside this repository (where User is constructed and where the tenant path parameter is handled), so exploitability cannot be settled from the available code. Separately, wipe at src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, which returns a boolean that is discarded, so wipe has no authorization check at all; that is a stronger, separate defect the candidate did not mention.
